posts.raw_content:
Surveillance Technology: FalcoNet
Cognyte is the manufacturer of FalcoNet, a controversial cell-site simulator (IMSI catcher) used for mobile phone surveillance. 

Functionality: FalcoNet mimics a legitimate cell tower, forcing nearby mobile phones (2G through 5G) to connect to it instead of the carrier network. This allows operators to capture device identifiers (IMSI/IMEI) and location data from all phones in range, not just specific targets. Cognyte is used for surveillance primarily through two distinct methods: active signal interception using hardware devices and passive data fusion using software analytics. 

Active Signal Interception (IMSI Catchers)
The most direct form of surveillance is conducted using FalcoNet, an IMSI-catcher (also known as a cell-site simulator) similar to the widely known "Stingray." 

Mechanism: The device mimics a legitimate cell tower, broadcasting a signal strong enough to force nearby mobile phones (2G through 5G) to disconnect from real towers and connect to it instead. 
Data Collection: Once connected, FalcoNet harvests unique identifiers (IMSI, IMEI) and precise location data from every device in range, not just specific targets.  This creates a "dragnet" effect, collecting data on innocent bystanders alongside suspects.
Deployment: The system is highly portable and modular. Recent contracts reveal it is being deployed in:
Vehicles: Concealed inside police SUVs (e.g., Chevy Tahoes used by Texas and Florida police) to track movements while driving.
Airborne: Mounted on helicopters for wide-area surveillance, such as monitoring migration routes.
Portable: Packaged in backpacks for foot patrols or tactical operations. 
Stealth: The technology operates silently without the user's knowledge, and the hardware can be hidden behind false vehicle roofs to remain visually indistinguishable from standard patrol cars
